title: Claims quality report
prompt: Every claims load ends with a quality report. Write `solve(claims)` so it returns one row per rule below, with the rule's name in `rule` and the number of claims that break it in `failed`.
rules: `dates_in_order`: both dates are present and `service_date` is not after `submitted_date`.
`allowed_within_billed`: `allowed_amount` is missing, or `billed_amount` is present and at least as large.
`paid_amount_matches_status`: `paid` and `denied` claims have a `paid_amount`; claims with any other status don't.
Return all three rules, even when nothing fails. `failed` is a whole number of type bigint.
hints: Keep the rules as a list of `(name, condition)` pairs, each true for a good claim, and loop over them.
Count failures with `claims.filter(~F.coalesce(passes, F.lit(False))).count()`, so a NULL rule counts as a failure.
Collect `(name, failed)` tuples in a list and build the result with `spark.createDataFrame(results, "rule STRING, failed BIGINT")`.
